findings.title: Login-cache invalidation can be skipped for IDPs in a disabled organization
findings.body: registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate evaluates getLoginPredicate() against original, which is obtained via getById(). getById() returns createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel(), whose isEnabled() returns false when the IDP's organization is disabled (or the organization provider is disabled). The login cache, however, is populated from idpDelegate.getForLogin(), which filters the raw stored IDP and does not consider organization enabled state, so an org-linked IDP can still be present in the cached list while original tests as not login-eligible. If an update changes hideOnLogin, enabled, or BROKER_PUBLIC while the organization is disabled, both original and updated predicates can evaluate false and the method returns without invalidating any login cache. After the organization is re-enabled, the stale cached ID remains and a hidden/non-public IDP can be returned to login pages. The predicate should be evaluated against the raw stored model rather than the organization-aware wrapper, or org enabled state must be part of the invalidation decision.

findings.title: Test cleanup registers removal for literal alias "alias", leaking created IDPs
findings.body: The cleanup registered here (and again at line 425) is testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove, using the literal string "alias" instead of the loop's alias variable. It therefore tries to remove a non-existent IDP rather than the IDPs created by the test. The created IDPs, including ones linked to the shared test-realm organization, remain after the test and can change counts/assertions in other OrganizationCacheTest methods or later tests, making the suite order-dependent. Use the actual alias and avoid double-removal for idp-alias-1, which is removed inline.

findings.title: New test does not cover create/remove invalidation for login-eligible IDPs
findings.body: testCacheIDPForLogin only exercises the non-invalidating create/remove paths: it creates a hidden IDP and removes a disabled IDP, then verifies the login caches remain. It never verifies that creating or removing an IDP that does qualify for login invalidates the per-mode login caches. A regression in the registerIDPLoginInvalidation() calls from create() or remove() would therefore not be caught by this test.
